answer: An auditor observes that a jade certificate issues only after the registrar sees a nadir reading, meaning the credential fell to its lowest recorded activity and stayed for one full interval. The reading is signed by the ledger, not self-reported, and binds a crystal commitment whose preimage must be revealed later to claim any balance. Replicas that burst activity never produce a nadir reading, so their balance has no valid certificate and is void at settlement. Violations show as a mismatch between claimed balance and the deepest signed quiet period on record.
